title: Optimizing Quantum Circuit Mapping to Reduce Inter-Module Communications in Distributed Architectures
problem: Modular quantum architectures require mapping circuits to distributed modules; non-local operations incur significant communication overhead limiting scalability.
motivation: Quantum computing requires modular architectures for scalability; optimizing circuit mapping to minimize inter-module communication is critical.
method: DQTetris: hierarchical framework seeking global communication-free qubit mapping, then layer-wise gate pruning for subcircuits with adaptive teleportation.
key_novelty: Communication overhead reduction via optimal circuit segmentation and adaptive teleportation; 28-75% improvement over existing methods.
contributions: Hierarchical global and local qubit mapping framework
Layer-wise gate pruning for subcircuit isolation
Adaptive gate teleportation to minimize reassignment events
28-75% communication cost reduction vs. existing methods
limitations: Quantum-specific; assumes module capacity constraints; limited to circuit-level optimization; practical validation on real quantum hardware needed.
